BiblicalUsage: In Aramaic this is simply the word for 'I', and it shows up in Daniel's mouth and in Nebuchadnezzar's: Daniel says the secret was not revealed to him for any wisdom he has more than any living, and the king, walking on his palace roof, boasts of the great Babylon he has built for the honour of his majesty. The same little word carries Daniel's humility and the king's pride in back-to-back chapters.
TheologicalSignificance: One small word for 'I' carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the contrast — Daniel's 'I' that points away from himself, and Nebuchadnezzar's 'I' that points only at himself.
